title: Make the escalate disarm actually disarm a legacy ceiling cell
action: Fix the silent no-op (r3 P2, corroborated by both reviewers; decisions escalate-off-disarm D1/D2). RED FIRST: write a test proving the current failure - a cell with tier ceiling plus escalate:true, disarmed via set_escalation false, still answers cell_is_escalated true - run it against unfixed code and quote the red in the cap. Then: (1) validate.rs cell_is_escalated: an explicit Some(Bool(false)) on ESCALATE_FIELD returns false BEFORE the legacy tier read; (2) session_preamble/store.rs map_is_escalated: the same explicit-false arm, same ordering; (3) handlers_close.rs set_escalation disarm arm: when the cell carries tier == ESCALATION_WORD write Bool(false), otherwise remove the key as today; (4) handlers_write.rs backfill plan derivation: skip escalate when the ESCALATE_FIELD key is PRESENT with either value, so a recorded disarm is never re-armed by a later pass. Tests: the red-first disarm test goes green; backfill does not re-arm an explicitly disarmed legacy cell; an ordinary (no-tier) cell disarm still removes the key; a bare tier-ceiling cell with no flag still reads escalated (pre-backfill compat); the ration counter and the preamble counter agree with the dispatch on a disarmed legacy cell.

truths: The red-first test fails on unfixed code and its output is quoted in the cap
Disarming a legacy tier-ceiling cell makes cell_is_escalated, the preamble counter, and the dispatch all answer not-escalated
A later backfill-roles run leaves an explicitly disarmed legacy cell disarmed
An ordinary cell disarm still removes the key entirely
A bare tier-ceiling cell with no flag key still reads escalated
Re-arming with escalate on still works and the 40 percent ration still gates it

trace.outcome: escalate disarm now actually disarms a legacy ceiling cell; an explicit escalate:false outranks the legacy tier read everywhere and survives later backfill passes
deviations: Executed inline instead of via a dispatched execution worker; reason recorded as trace.inline_reason.
